study_type_evidence.quote: We first evaluated the in-vivo efficacy of DTX-P7 in a mouse xenograft model of A549 cells.
A549 cells were treated with 0, 10, 50 nM DTX-P7 or 1 nM DTX for 48 h followed by total RNA extraction and real-time PCR

in_vivo_species.strain_sex_age: not reported (strain, sex and age are not stated in the body; animals are described only as A549 or A549/CD133+ xenograft tumor-bearing mice)
in_vivo_species.quote: A549 tumor-bearing mice were randomized to receive intraperitoneal injection of vehicle control, 10 mg/kg DTX-P7, 20 mg/kg DTX-P7 or 10 mg/kg DTX once a week for 4 weeks

in_vitro_detail: A549 and A549/CD133+ cell culture: Western blotting and real-time PCR for Hsp90, cycloheximide chase of Hsp90 turnover, co-treatment with bafilomycin A1 (10 nM) or bortezomib (20 nM), cytosol/membrane fractionation, label-free quantitative proteomics, PKH26 dye-dilution viability assay, propidium iodide cell-cycle analysis and HA-ubiquitin immunoprecipitation of DYRK1A.

agents.name: DTX-P7 (docetaxel-heptapeptide P7 conjugate)
agents.sequence_source: Introduction: 'we successfully identified a heptapeptide (LPLTPLP, namely P7) by phage display technique'
agents.chemical_identifier: structure shown in Additional file 2: Fig. S1; no CAS or catalogue number given in the body
agents.group_n: n = 5 mice/group (A549 model); n = 7 mice/group (A549/CD133+ model)
agents.group_n_quote: 10 mg/kg DTX-P7, 20 mg/kg DTX-P7 or 10 mg/kg DTX once a week for 4 weeks (n = 5 mice/group)
agents.dose: 10 and 20 mg/kg weekly x4 (A549 efficacy); 15 and 30 mg/kg weekly x4 (A549/CD133+ efficacy); 60 mg/kg single dose (biodistribution)
agents.dose_route_quote: A549 tumor-bearing mice were injected intraperitoneally with 30 mg/kg DTX or 60 mg/kg DTX-P7 followed by determination of distribution of DTX or DTX-P7 in tumor specimens throughout 72 h.
agents.pk_quote: To investigate the targeting characteristics of DTX-P7, the biodistribution of both DTX and DTX-P7 was analyzed by high-performance liquid chromatography.

bioanalytical_quote: the biodistribution of both DTX and DTX-P7 was analyzed by high-performance liquid chromatography
notes: NO PHARMACOKINETIC DATA IN THE BODY. The body reports no half-life, Cmax, Tmax, AUC or plasma concentration for DTX-P7 or DTX; the abstract's claim of 'long circulation half-life' is not substantiated anywhere after '=== BODY ===' and so was not used. The only half-life mentioned in the body is that of the Hsp90 protein measured by cycloheximide chase in A549 cells ('Half-life of Hsp90 was determined using Image J software and plotted against treatment time'), which is a protein-turnover measurement, not drug PK. The mouse strain, sex and age are never stated in the body (the PEPLIFE2 header's 'BALB/c' was not used as evidence). This is a short 'To the editor' letter: the Methods section contains only data-availability and ethics statements, so no dosing formulation, sampling schedule, PK model or animal husbandry details are available. Additional in vitro tool compounds used but not itemised as agents: cycloheximide (2.5 mg/mL), bafilomycin A1 (10 nM), bortezomib (20 nM), PKH26 dye and HA-ubiquitin transfection. The file header shows 'PMID: ?' with PMC9164557; the PMID was supplied by the assignment.
